literal: Hong alone did not accept Shao's gifts; from Changsun Song down all were ashamed.
idiomatic: Hong alone refused Shao's gifts; from Changsun Song downward the courtiers were ashamed.

literal: An edict sent envoys to tour the commanderies and kingdoms to investigate governors and magistrates who failed the law, ordering Hong together with the Duke of Yidu, Mu Guan, and others to review them; the emperor praised their fairness.
idiomatic: An edict sent envoys through the commanderies to investigate lawless officials; Hong and the Duke of Yidu, Mu Guan, and others were ordered to judge the cases, and the emperor praised their fairness.

literal: Another edict ordered Hong with Changsun Song and others to decide criminal cases in the hall of court.
idiomatic: Another edict set Hong with Changsun Song and others to decide criminal cases in open court.

literal: Mingyuan, because powerful magnates in the commanderies and kingdoms were harming the realm, issued a generous edict summoning them.
idiomatic: Mingyuan, seeing great local magnates ruining the realm, issued a gentle edict summoning them in.

literal: Many clung to their homelands while local chiefs forced them to go.
idiomatic: Many wished to stay home while local chiefs drove them onward.

literal: Thereupon frivolous youths stirred one another and bands gathered everywhere.
idiomatic: Then idle youths incited one another and bands formed everywhere.

literal: In Xihé and Jianxing bandits rose together; governors could not suppress them.
idiomatic: Bandits rose together in Xihé and Jianxing; local officials could not stop them.

literal: The emperor then summoned Hong and the Marquis of Beixin, An Tong, the Marquis of Shouguang, Shusun Jian, the Marquis of Wuyuan, Yuan Qu, and others to ask their counsel.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned Hong, Marquis An Tong of Beixin, Marquis Shusun Jian of Shouguang, Marquis Yuan Qu of Wuyuan, and others for counsel.

literal: Hong wished a great amnesty to ease the crisis.
idiomatic: Hong urged a general amnesty to ease the crisis.

literal: Qu said, "Better first execute the ringleaders and pardon their followers.
idiomatic: Qu said, "Better first execute the ringleaders and pardon the rest.

literal: " Hong said, "A king facing the realm takes securing the people as his root—why fret over petty right and wrong?
idiomatic: Hong said, "A king holds the realm by keeping the people secure—why cling to petty right and wrong?

literal: Amnesty is not the straight path, yet it may be used as expedient.
idiomatic: Amnesty is not orthodox policy, yet it may serve as expedient.

literal: If after pardon they do not reform, execution will not be late.
idiomatic: If after pardon they do not reform, punishment can wait no longer.

literal: " Mingyuan followed this.
idiomatic: Mingyuan accepted Hong's view.

literal: At the beginning of Shenrui an edict set Hong with the Duke of Nanping, Song, and others to sit and halt at the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate and hear weighty affairs.
idiomatic: Early in Shenrui an edict seated Hong with the Duke of Nanping, Song, and others at the right of the Chariot-Halting Gate to hear state business.

literal: Tens of thousands of Hu in Bing Province raided south into Henei; the emperor sent the general Gongsun Biao and others to attack them and they were defeated.
idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Hu from Bing Province raided south into Henei; the general Gongsun Biao and others were sent against them and were beaten.

literal: The emperor asked the ministers for a plan.
idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers for counsel.

literal: Hong said, "Biao's armies and the rest are not insufficient—they only failed in disposition, so petty bandits gained a breathing space.
idiomatic: Hong said, "Biao's forces were ample—they only mishandled deployment, letting petty raiders catch their breath.

literal: Though the Hu are many, they have no fierce, able commander-in-chief—what is called a thousand slaves sharing one beam.
idiomatic: Though the Hu are numerous, they lack a fierce chief—they are like a thousand slaves sharing one rafter.

literal: One should get a great general long trusted by the Hu, lead several hundred horsemen, go and take command of Biao's army to strike them.
idiomatic: Send a great general the Hu have long trusted, with a few hundred horsemen, to take over Biao's army and strike them.

literal: When the bandits hear it they will surely tremble in fear at the wind.
idiomatic: At the news the raiders will surely break in terror.

literal: Marquis Shusun Jian, formerly in Bing Province, was unmatched among the generals.
idiomatic: Marquis Shusun Jian, who once held Bing Province, outshone every general there.

literal: " The emperor followed this and thereupon pacified the Hu raiders.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and the Hu raiders were pacified.

literal: Soon he was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Grandee of the Heavenly Division and raised to duke.

literal: In summer of the third year of Taichang, Hong's illness grew grave; the emperor sent the Palace Attendant Mu Guan to receive his last words; attendants inquired after his health and returned several times in one night.
idiomatic: In summer of Taichang year three, Hong grew desperately ill; the emperor sent Palace Attendant Mu Guan for his final counsel; attendants called through the night again and again.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Duke Wen Zhen.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.

literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.
idiomatic: His funeral wholly followed the precedent of Prince Ancheng, Shusun Jun.

literal: An edict ordered all ministers and attached tribal chieftains to attend the burial; from princes down all were commanded to bow in farewell.
idiomatic: An edict required all ministers and subject tribal chiefs to attend; every rank below the princes was ordered to bow him forth.

literal: His son Hao succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Hao succeeded.

literal: In the Taihe era Xiaowen recorded the merit of the former court and granted Hong a place in the temple sacrifice.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era Xiaowen honored founders of the prior reign and gave Hong a place in the ancestral temple.

literal: Hao, style name Boshen, in youth loved learning.
idiomatic: Hao, styled Boshen, loved learning from youth.

literal: He broadly read classics and histories, dark signs, yin-yang, and the hundred schools—nothing escaped his survey.
idiomatic: He read widely in classics, histories, astronomy, yin-yang, and the hundred schools.

literal: Probing essence and principle, none of the age could match him.
idiomatic: Probing principle to the root, none of his day could match him.

literal: At twenty he was Direct Attendant; he was gradually promoted to Compiler.
idiomatic: At twenty he was Direct Attendant and later rose to Compiler.

literal: Daowu, because of his skill at calligraphy, kept him constantly at his side.
idiomatic: Daowu kept him always near, for his skill at calligraphy.

literal: In Daowu's last years his majesty grew stern; many in the palace staff were punished for slight faults, and all fled and hid the changes before their eyes.
idiomatic: In Daowu's last years his wrath was sharp; palace staff were punished for trifles and all hid what they saw.

literal: Hao alone was respectful and diligent without slackening, sometimes not returning home for a whole day.
idiomatic: Hao alone stayed respectful and diligent, sometimes not leaving court for a full day.

literal: When the emperor learned of it he would order imperial gruel bestowed.
idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it he sent imperial gruel.

literal: His upright bearing in office and refusal to change with fortune or ruin were like this.
idiomatic: Such was his upright service and refusal to bend with fortune or ruin.

literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was made Libationer of the Erudites and enfeoffed Viscount of Wucheng.
idiomatic: At Mingyuan's accession he was made Libationer of the Erudites and enfeoffed Viscount of Wucheng.

literal: He regularly taught the emperor the classics; whenever they went to suburban sacrifice, father and son both rode in light carriages—the age envied them.
idiomatic: He regularly taught the emperor the classics; at each suburban sacrifice father and son rode in light carriages, to the envy of the court.

literal: Mingyuan loved yin-yang and numerology; hearing Hao explain the Changes and the Great Plan's Five Phases, he was pleased.
idiomatic: Mingyuan loved yin-yang and numerology; pleased by Hao's lectures on the Changes and the Five Phases of the Great Plan,

literal: He then ordered divination of fortune and ill, joint observation of the heavens, and fixing of doubtful matters.
idiomatic: he ordered Hao to divine fortune, scan the heavens, and settle doubtful matters.

literal: Hao grasped the junction of Heaven and man and set forth their guiding threads; many families had verified results.
idiomatic: Hao mastered the meeting of Heaven and man and laid out their patterns; many of his forecasts proved true.

literal: He was constantly joined to the great plans of army and state and was deeply favored in secret.
idiomatic: He was constantly drawn into army and state plans and enjoyed deep, secret favor.

literal: At the time a hare appeared in the rear palace and search found no way it could have entered; the emperor ordered Hao to deduce it.
idiomatic: A hare then appeared in the inner palace with no entry found; the emperor had Hao reason it out.

literal: Hao judged that a neighboring state would present a tribute concubine.
idiomatic: Hao said a neighboring state would soon send a tribute woman.

literal: The next year Yao Xing indeed presented a daughter.
idiomatic: The next year Yao Xing did present a daughter.

literal: In the second year of Shenrui the autumn grain failed; the Grand Astrologer Wang Liang and Su Tan, through Princess Huayin and others, said, "Prognostic books say the state should move its capital to Ye and great music for fifty years.
idiomatic: In Shenrui year two the autumn crop failed; Grand Astrologers Wang Liang and Su Tan, through Princess Huayin and others, said, "Prognostic books say the capital should move to Ye and great fortune for fifty years.

literal: " They urged the emperor to move the capital to Ye to relieve this year's famine.
idiomatic: They urged moving the capital to Ye to ease the famine.

literal: The emperor asked Hao.
idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao.

literal: Hao said, "That is not a long-term plan.
idiomatic: Hao said, "That is no lasting policy.

literal: The people of the eastern provinces constantly say the state dwells in a vast waste, men and beasts beyond counting, called a host like ox-hair.
idiomatic: Easterners constantly say we live in boundless wastes, with men and beasts beyond count, like ox-hair on a hide.

literal: Now if the old capital is left guarded while families move south, I fear they will not fill the lands of the commanderies.
idiomatic: If we leave the old capital lightly held while families move south, they may not even fill the eastern commanderies.

literal: Scattered among counties, dwelling beneath scrub forest, unaccustomed to soil and water, plague and death will show the matter plainly; the people's will will falter.
idiomatic: Set among counties under scrub and forest, unfit for soil and water, sickness and death will expose the plan and hearts will fail.

literal: When the four quarters hear it they will hold us in light contempt; Juqu and the Rouran will surely seize the moment and come.
idiomatic: When the realm hears, contempt will follow; Juqu and the Rouran will surely press in.

literal: Yunzhong and Pingcheng will face peril; Heng and Dai cut off, a thousand li apart—rescue will be desperately hard.
idiomatic: Yunzhong and Pingcheng will be in peril; Heng and Dai cut off a thousand li away, rescue will come too late.

literal: Thus fame and substance will both suffer.
idiomatic: Fame and strength will both be lost.

literal: To dwell in the north now—suppose the east should stir, light horse can ride south and blaze glory in the homeland—who knows how many would submit?
idiomatic: Dwelling in the north, if the east should stir, light cavalry can ride south and awe the homeland—who knows how many would bow?

literal: When the people see it they will turn to dust in fear and submission.
idiomatic: The people would see them and tremble into submission.

literal: This is the state's long strategy for commanding the Huaxia.
idiomatic: That is the long strategy for ruling the Huaxia.

literal: When spring grass grows and dairy and cheese come forth, with vegetables and fruit as well, it will suffice until the coming autumn.
idiomatic: When spring grass returns and dairy comes, with vegetables and fruit besides, we can hold until autumn.

literal: If the middle harvest succeeds, the matter is saved.
idiomatic: If the mid-year crop succeeds, the crisis passes.

literal: " The emperor deeply agreed.
idiomatic: The emperor was fully convinced.

literal: He again sent a palace favorite to ask Hao, "Now we have nothing to carry us to next autumn, or the crop may again fail—what then?
idiomatic: He again sent a palace officer to ask Hao, "We may not last until next autumn, or the crop may fail again—what then?

literal: " Hao said, "Select the poorest households and send the commanderies to gather grain where it may be found.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Relieve the poorest households and send the commanderies to gather grain where it exists.

literal: If autumn brings no harvest, we may plan again—but the capital must not be moved.
idiomatic: If autumn fails, we can plan anew—but do not move the capital.

literal: " The emperor thereupon divided people to seek food in the three eastern provinces and opened granaries to supply them.
idiomatic: The emperor then sent people to the three eastern provinces for grain and opened storehouses to feed them.

literal: The next year brought a great harvest; Hao was given a concubine each and imperial robes of silk and cotton.
idiomatic: The next year brought abundance; Hao received a concubine each and imperial silks.

literal: Earlier, in the year before Yao Xing's death, the astrologers reported Mars in the Dipper constellation; one night it suddenly vanished, none knew where.
idiomatic: Earlier, the year before Yao Xing died, astrologers reported Mars in the Dipper; one night it vanished, none knew where.

literal: Some said it had entered a state on the brink of ruin and would bring children's songs and strange talk before the disaster struck.
idiomatic: Some said it had entered a doomed state and would bring ballads and omens before disaster fell.

literal: The emperor summoned eminent Confucians and the clerks to seek where it had gone.
idiomatic: The emperor summoned leading scholars and clerks to find its course.

literal: Hao replied, "According to the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a spirit descended on Mount Cui, on the day of arrival each thing had its sign.
idiomatic: Hao replied, "The Zuo Commentary says when a spirit descended on Mount Cui, on the day of arrival each thing had its sign.

literal: Please calculate by day and branch.
idiomatic: Calculate by the day and its branches.

literal: On the evening of gengwu and the morning of xinwei the sky was cloudy; Mars's disappearance should fall within these two days.
idiomatic: On the evening of gengwu and morning of xinwei the sky was overcast; Mars's vanishing should fall within those two days.

literal: Geng and wu both belong to Qin; xin is the western barbarians.
idiomatic: Geng and wu both belong to Qin; xin marks the western Yi.

literal: Now Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.
idiomatic: Yao Xing holds Xianyang—Mars has entered Qin.

literal: " All changed color and said, "A star lost in heaven—how can a man know where it goes and speak groundless words!
idiomatic: All flushed and said, "A star is lost in heaven—how can a man know its path and speak without proof!

literal: " Hao smiled and did not answer.
idiomatic: Hao smiled and said nothing.

literal: After more than eighty days Mars indeed came forth at the Well constellation and lingered there.
idiomatic: After eighty-odd days Mars indeed appeared at the Well and lingered there.

literal: In Qin a great drought scorched the land; the Kunming Pool dried up.
idiomatic: Qin suffered great drought; the Kunming Pool ran dry.

literal: Children's ballads and false talk made the realm clamorous.
idiomatic: Ballads and rumors threw the realm into uproar.

literal: The next year Yao Xing died; his two sons fought each other and in three years the state perished.
idiomatic: The next year Yao Xing died; his two sons fought and in three years the state was gone.

literal: Thereupon all were convinced.
idiomatic: Then all were convinced.

literal: In the first year of Taichang the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, wishing to ascend the river westward and request passage.
idiomatic: In Taichang year one the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong and asked to march up the river west with passage granted.

literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate.
idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation among the ministers.

literal: The outer court dukes and ministers all said, "Hangu Pass is heaven's barrier—how can Yu enter west?
idiomatic: The outer court said, "Hangu Pass is heaven's rampart—how could Yu enter the west?

literal: He proclaims attack on Yao but his intent may be hard to fathom.
idiomatic: He claims to attack Yao but his aim may be obscure.

literal: We should first send troops to cut the upper river and not let him pass west.
idiomatic: Send troops first to block the upper river and forbid his westward march.

literal: " The inner court wholly agreed with the outer plan; the emperor was about to follow it.
idiomatic: The inner court agreed; the emperor was ready to follow.

literal: Hao said, "This is not the superior plan.
idiomatic: Hao said, "That is not the best course.

literal: Sima Xiuzhi and his faction are harrying Jing Province; Liu Yu has long gnashed his teeth.
idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi's faction troubles Jing Province; Liu Yu has long burned for revenge.

literal: Now with Xing dead and the heir young, striking their peril and ruin—by my reading he is sure to enter the Pass himself.
idiomatic: With Xing dead and the heir a child, he will seize their weakness—I read his intent as certain entry into the Pass.

literal: A man fierce and rash does not look to later trouble.
idiomatic: Men fierce and rash do not weigh later harm.

literal: If we now block his western road, Yu will surely come ashore and raid north.
idiomatic: Block his western road now and Yu will surely land and raid north.

literal: Then Yao will be unharmed while we bear the blow.
idiomatic: Then Yao is untouched while we take the blow.

literal: The Rouran raid within; grain is again scarce—send troops south and the northern foe advances;
idiomatic: The Rouran raid within and grain runs short—send armies south and the northern enemy presses in;

literal: if we rescue the north, the southern provinces are again in peril—better grant passage on the waterway and let Yu go west.
idiomatic: rescue the north and the south is endangered again—better grant the water road and let Yu go west.

literal: Then raise troops to block his road east when he returns.
idiomatic: Then raise troops to block his road home to the east.

literal: This is what is called Bian Zhuang stabbing the leopard and gaining both—
idiomatic: This is Bian Zhuang stabbing the leopard—gaining both at once—
